provenance.purpose: Research projection for the Bible map; retains every coordinate resolution and unresolved interpretation in the recorded geographic source.
provenance.creator: OpenBible.info
provenance.osmGeometryLicense: ODbL 1.0 where OpenStreetMap geometry is used
provenance.coordinateOrder: lon, lat; decimal degrees as supplied by OpenBible
provenance.sourceResolutionReferences: Zero-based [identification index, resolution index] in the ancient source record.
provenance.sourceRanking: Unchanged modern_associations score. Internal ordering only; do not display as evidence strength or a probability.
provenance.deduplication: Merged only repeated resolutions with matching modern ID, coordinates, coordinate type, description, spatial modifier, geometry ID, radius and feature type. Kept every identification description and source index.
provenance.verification: All source IDs match the 1,285 geography-bearing site nodes. All coordinate pairs have valid ranges and exactly match their linked modern source record. This is source-preserving data validation, not an independent archaeological verification of 1,285 identifications.
provenance.nameSelection: Prefer the catalog name when labeled modern; otherwise select a supplied modern name. Retain the catalog label and alternatives. If no modern name exists, retain the source label with a note.

coordinateTypes.point: Site or feature point; precision metadata still applies and does not establish the ancient identification.
coordinateTypes.representative point: A point used to represent a larger region or linear feature.
coordinateTypes.center: A center for an approximate area; retain the stated radius.
coordinateTypes.settlement: A containing settlement used because no more specific coordinates are supplied for the feature.

provenance.display: One source-listed location per place is shown initially. Source modern-association scores order candidates internally, with source order for ties; scores are not displayed. All alternatives and unresolved interpretations remain accessible. Point precision is not certainty of ancient identification.

places.locationNote: the identification of Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor) with "Khirbet Gadeirah, north of el-Jib" is possibly Jedireh, as it’s located just northeast. However, it’s a modern settlement, not a ruin. Khirbet Judeira, on the other hand, which International Standard Bible Encyclopedia (1979) (Gedor) mentions as a possibility, is 10km west-northwest, not north. Other sources use Gibeon (i.e., El Jib) as a reference when referring to Jedireh but don’t call it a khirbet. Demsky, Genealogy of Gibeon (1971) (page 22), from 1971, supports the identification with Jedireh ("Perhaps Judeira, 3 kilometers northeast of El-Jib"); Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor)’s identification carries over unchanged from Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible (1975) (Gedor); however, Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible (1975) mentions both "modern Jedireh and Khirbet Gudeira," so on balance I think Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor) is probably referring to Khirbet Judeira

locations.name: Har Zin
precisionNotes: this appears to be the mountain referred to in the articles on Mount Hor, but it’s located 40 miles from Kadesh Barnea. However, the original source for this claim (Trumbull, Kadesh-Barnea: Its Importance and Probable Site (1884)), I think, places it at this point instead: "near the western extemity of the Wady Feqreh" (page 132), or Nahal Zin (Aharoni, Land of the Bible (1979)). It is also "southwest of the passes Es-Sufah and El-Yemen" (page 132) and near "the border wadies--Feqreh, Madurah, Murrah, and Hanjoorat" (page 133). All except the last are visible in this area on Palestine Exploration Fund Old and New Testament Map (1898). Similarly, Burton, Biblical World, volume 31 (1908) (page 88) places it "twenty-five miles southwest of the southern end of the Dead Sea... If a line, therefore, were drawn from Ain Kadees to the southern end of the Dead Sea, Jebel Maderah would stand at about the middle point." Coupled with other sources identifying this mountain as the possible burial place of Aaron (e.g., Wikipedia), I think the "15 miles" figure is off or is not using Ain el Qudeirat as the location for Kadesh-barnea

However, the original source for this claim (Trumbull, Kadesh-Barnea: Its Importance and Probable Site (1884)), I think, places it at this point instead: "near the western extemity of the Wady Feqreh" (page 132), or Nahal Zin (Aharoni, Land of the Bible (1979)). It is also "southwest of the passes Es-Sufah and El-Yemen" (page 132) and near "the border wadies--Feqreh, Madurah, Murrah, and Hanjoorat" (page 133). All except the last are visible in this area on Palestine Exploration Fund Old and New Testament Map (1898). Similarly, Burton, Biblical World, volume 31 (1908) (page 88) places it "twenty-five miles southwest of the southern end of the Dead Sea... If a line, therefore, were drawn from Ain Kadees to the southern end of the Dead Sea, Jebel Maderah would stand at about the middle point." locations.name: Har Zin
precisionNotes: this appears to be the mountain referred to in the articles on Mount Hor, but it’s located 40 miles from Kadesh Barnea. However, the original source for this claim (Trumbull, Kadesh-Barnea: Its Importance and Probable Site (1884)), I think, places it at this point instead: "near the western extemity of the Wady Feqreh" (page 132), or Nahal Zin (Aharoni, Land of the Bible (1979)). It is also "southwest of the passes Es-Sufah and El-Yemen" (page 132) and near "the border wadies--Feqreh, Madurah, Murrah, and Hanjoorat" (page 133). All except the last are visible in this area on Palestine Exploration Fund Old and New Testament Map (1898). Similarly, Burton, Biblical World, volume 31 (1908) (page 88) places it "twenty-five miles southwest of the southern end of the Dead Sea... If a line, therefore, were drawn from Ain Kadees to the southern end of the Dead Sea, Jebel Maderah would stand at about the middle point." Coupled with other sources identifying this mountain as the possible burial place of Aaron (e.g., Wikipedia), I think the "15 miles" figure is off or is not using Ain el Qudeirat as the location for Kadesh-barnea

locations.name: Har Zin
precisionNotes: this appears to be the mountain referred to in the articles on Mount Hor, but it’s located 40 miles from Kadesh Barnea. However, the original source for this claim (Trumbull, Kadesh-Barnea: Its Importance and Probable Site (1884)), I think, places it at this point instead: "near the western extemity of the Wady Feqreh" (page 132), or Nahal Zin (Aharoni, Land of the Bible (1979)). It is also "southwest of the passes Es-Sufah and El-Yemen" (page 132) and near "the border wadies--Feqreh, Madurah, Murrah, and Hanjoorat" (page 133). All except the last are visible in this area on Palestine Exploration Fund Old and New Testament Map (1898). Similarly, Burton, Biblical World, volume 31 (1908) (page 88) places it "twenty-five miles southwest of the southern end of the Dead Sea... If a line, therefore, were drawn from Ain Kadees to the southern end of the Dead Sea, Jebel Maderah would stand at about the middle point." Coupled with other sources identifying this mountain as the possible burial place of Aaron (e.g., Wikipedia), I think the "15 miles" figure is off or is not using Ain el Qudeirat as the location for Kadesh-barnea

locations.name: Har Zin
precisionNotes: this appears to be the mountain referred to in the articles on Mount Hor, but it’s located 40 miles from Kadesh Barnea. However, the original source for this claim (Trumbull, Kadesh-Barnea: Its Importance and Probable Site (1884)), I think, places it at this point instead: "near the western extemity of the Wady Feqreh" (page 132), or Nahal Zin (Aharoni, Land of the Bible (1979)). It is also "southwest of the passes Es-Sufah and El-Yemen" (page 132) and near "the border wadies--Feqreh, Madurah, Murrah, and Hanjoorat" (page 133). All except the last are visible in this area on Palestine Exploration Fund Old and New Testament Map (1898). Similarly, Burton, Biblical World, volume 31 (1908) (page 88) places it "twenty-five miles southwest of the southern end of the Dead Sea... If a line, therefore, were drawn from Ain Kadees to the southern end of the Dead Sea, Jebel Maderah would stand at about the middle point." Coupled with other sources identifying this mountain as the possible burial place of Aaron (e.g., Wikipedia), I think the "15 miles" figure is off or is not using Ain el Qudeirat as the location for Kadesh-barnea
